paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's church is not a casual hangout. Paul says it is "God’s household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth" (1 Timothy 3:15). So the people who lead it and serve in it carry something precious, and that's why Paul lists out what their lives should look like (1 Timothy 3:2-13).

Notice what's on that list. Gentle, self-controlled, hospitable, honest with their words, faithful at home, and tested before they serve. Not one line says "must be famous" or "must be flashy." Paul cares about who a person is when nobody's clapping, and he says those who serve well gain "a high standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus" (1 Timothy 3:13). Whether you ever hold an office or not, friend, I think this list is a mirror worth standing in front of, and I know I'm checking my own mustache in it.

And then Paul lands the plane. All of this conduct points to Jesus, because "the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory" (1 Timothy 3:16). We live well because of WHO we belong to, not to earn a spot. So bake your life with care, friend, because the household you're in belongs to Him.
